answer: Each agent mints one ferrous seal that binds its key to one work sample, is non-transferable, and expires at the horizon. Minting burns a fee from a spiral schedule: the kth seal this horizon burns 30+2(k-1) credits, so the 1000th burns 2028 and 1000 seals burn 1029000 in fees plus 50000 in 50-credit bonds, each bond returned after a clean horizon. Auditors check seal, key, and sample match; a rented-seal ring fails because a rented seal carries another key, so its sample mismatches and its bond burns. An honest agent pays one fee and locks one bond, recovering it after a clean horizon.
